must_fix.title: Dialog focus trap includes hidden elements, so Tab escapes the dialog (e.g. with a Tabs inside)
must_fix.evidence: getFocusables (src/Dialog.tsx:20-34) is a pure CSS selector and doesn't exclude [hidden] or non-rendered elements; TabPanel always has tabIndex=0 and is merely `hidden` (src/Tabs.tsx:175-176). Probe: <Dialog open title="T"><button>One</button><Tabs defaultValue="a">…<TabPanel value="a">pa</TabPanel><TabPanel value="b">pb</TabPanel></Tabs></Dialog>; focus 'pa', user.tab() -> 'after Tab from last visible: <body>…' (focus left the dialog); focus 'One', user.tab({shift:true}) -> 'after shift-tab from first: <div role="tabpanel" id="«r1»-panel-b" … tabindex="0"' (a hidden panel). Contradicts the issue's 'traps it there' and README 'Focus never leaves the dialog'. Needs a fix plus a regression test.

nits: The README says the first Escape on an open Combobox inside a Dialog only closes the popup; this works (I checked it with a probe), but no test in the repo covers it.
tsconfig.json includes a `tests` directory and an empty tests/ folder exists, but the new tests live next to the code in src/ — possibly not the layout the repo intended.
Combobox never calls onChange(null), so once an option is chosen a user cannot clear the selection; this is documented as intentional but limits the `| null` part of the issue.
The listbox has no accessible name (e.g. aria-labelledby pointing at the label).
The 'No results' role=status region is added to the page at the same moment as its text, so some screen readers won't announce it.
On the very first render (before the layout effect), Tabs shows no selected tab or panel, which matters for server-side rendering.

report:
This isn't ready to merge yet: there is one must-fix bug in the Dialog's focus trap. `pnpm test` passes (63 tests in 3 files) and `pnpm typecheck` passes with no errors. Tabs and Combobox matched the issue in every case I tried. ## Must fix **The Dialog focus trap counts hidden elements, so Tab can leave the dialog.** `getFocusables` (`src/Dialog.tsx:20-34`) finds tabbable elements with a CSS selector only, so it also picks up elements that are `hidden` or not displayed. This library's own `TabPanel` always has `tabIndex={0}` and is only hidden when not selected (`src/Tabs.tsx:175-176`). So a dialog containing `Tabs` treats a hidden panel as its last focusable element: - Pressing Tab on the last visible element doesn't match `active === last`, so the browser's normal Tab behaviour runs and focus leaves the dialog. - Pressing Shift+Tab on the first element "wraps" to `last.focus()`, which is the hidden panel. I reproduced this with a probe test in a scratch directory, using this repo's vitest setup and `@testing-library/user-event`: ```tsx render(<> {}} title="T"> AB papb ); screen.getByText("pa").focus(); await user.tab(); screen.getByText("One").focus(); await user.tab({ shift: true }); ``` Output: ``` after Tab from last visible:
`, outside the dialog. After Shift+Tab it is on the hidden panel for tab "b". This breaks the issue's requirement that the dialog traps focus. It also contradicts the README line "Focus never leaves the dialog". The fix is to skip elements inside a `[hidden]` ancestor (or ones not rendered), and to add a test with `Tabs` inside a `Dialog`. ## Checked and working - **Tabs:** arrow keys wrap and skip disabled tabs, and Home and End work. Focus and selection still behave correctly under `StrictMode`. - **Dialog:** Escape and backdrop clicks close it, nested dialogs behave, and focus returns to the opener under `StrictMode`. - **Combobox:** filtering, `aria-activedescendant`, Enter, Escape and "No results" all work. Pressing Escape on an open Combobox inside a Dialog closes only the popup; a second Escape closes the dialog. `git status` is exactly as I found it.
